mechanism: A large one-hour BTC drawdown triggers stop-loss and liquidation-cascade selling in thinner-book alts that overshoots the alt's own BTC-implied beta -- alt order books are shallower and get swept by momentum-chasing/panic sellers and forced liquidations, pushing the alt further below fair value than BTC's own move justifies. That overshoot is unwound over the following hours as forced-selling flow exhausts and value-oriented buyers/arbitrageurs step back in, pulling the alt back toward BTC-implied fair value. This is the mirror-image economic story of row 106 (continuation after an up-shock, which this account's own train-era screen found refuted with entirely negative, opposite-sign net bps) -- it is a reversion/overreaction-correction mechanism specifically on the down-shock side, which the cited literature reports as asymmetric and stronger than the up-shock side.
counterparty: Retail momentum-chasers and forced/liquidation sellers who sell the alt into the panic low created by the BTC-shock cascade (getting the worst fill of the whole episode); they are the ones who transact at the overshot, stale-to-fair-value price and are the liquidity the reversion trade absorbs from as value buyers push price back up over the following hours.
prediction: Following an hour in which BTC's own return is below -60 bps, each of ETH/SOL/XRP/ADA (tested independently) shows a materially more positive mean forward return over the next 6 hours than its unconditional mean forward return over the same dataset -- i.e. the alt overshoots to the downside and then reverts, rather than continuing to fall. If the bootstrap CI95 on screened net bps (after the 11.5 bps cost) does not exclude zero, or WR < p*(150 bps) = 53.83% (fee_math.p_star), the thesis is falsified.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 106 (cross_asset_btc_shock_lag, this account's own prior run) traded a POSITIVE BTC shock as a continuation/momentum trigger (alt keeps drifting up with the shock) and was refuted with an entirely negative, opposite-sign CI on its own train data. This thesis instead reads the negative shock as a liquidation-cascade OVERSHOOT that then REVERTS -- a mean-reversion mechanism on the down side, not a continuation mechanism on the up side; row 106's own refutation (alt returns went negative after an up-shock rather than continuing up) is itself indirect evidence consistent with this thesis's reversion story, not a relabel of it.

Row 107 (cross_asset_ethbtc_regime_rotation) trades a slow multi-day ETH/BTC ratio trend-cross as a structural capital-rotation regime signal held for 48h. This thesis has no ratio, no trend-cross, and no multi-day rotation flow -- it is a single-bar shock trigger on BTC's own realized return, held for 6h, and the mechanism is order-book liquidation overshoot/correction, not fund-flow rotation.

Row 3 (1h vol-expansion fade) fades a volatility-expansion breakout in the SAME asset's own price/volatility history and died to single-split selection bias. This thesis's trigger is an exogenous asset's (BTC's) realized return, not the traded asset's own volatility regime, and the exit is a fixed 6h hold with a pre-registered ±20% tp_bps robustness read, not a discretionary fade of an in-sample breakout split.

Row 76 (multi-day MR / overnight window / vol-scaling) is dead post-2022 and uses a session/overnight boundary and vol-scaled sizing. This thesis has no overnight or session-boundary logic and no vol-scaled position sizing -- fixed $200 notional, fixed 6h hold, triggered purely by BTC's own prior closed-bar return crossing a threshold.

evidence: (1) PMC11602072 (top-20 cryptocurrencies by market cap, 6,606 daily observations, 2016-01-02 to 2021-04-15) reports a pre-pandemic reversal coefficient of +0.099 (t=6.59, significant at 1%), which the authors interpret as support for the overreaction hypothesis in crypto returns -- i.e. a documented, statistically significant reversal-after-overreaction effect in this exact asset class, at daily granularity, which this thesis stretches down to an hourly BTC-shock trigger with a 6-hour resolution window (a horizon-mismatch caveat, not a refutation: the direction of the effect -- overreaction followed by reversal -- is the one this thesis trades). (2) arxiv 2608.21888v1 ('Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets: a matched cross-market measurement', 183 Binance USDT pairs, Jan 2025-Feb 2026, 15-minute bars) independently confirms crypto-specific short-horizon mean reversion is real and statistically significant (class-mean AUC 0.531 vs 0.499 for US equities, 90% of crypto pairs significant after FDR control, incl. BTC AUC 0.533 p<1e-3, ETH 0.538 p<1e-3, XRP 0.536 p<1e-3) but explicitly flags it as fee-trapped at that granularity ('gross edge peaks near 1.3 bp per trade against a 5 bp round-trip cost') and reports the signal 'decays monotonically and is gone by four hours' -- both facts this thesis takes seriously: (a) the generic unconditional 15-min reversal this paper measures is far too small to clear this desk's 11.5 bps cost, which is exactly why this thesis conditions on a LARGE discrete BTC shock (>60bps/1h) rather than trading the small ambient reversion the paper measures, and (b) the paper's 'gone by four hours' decay profile is why this thesis registers a 6-hour hold rather than a multi-day one -- a longer hold would trade past the point this literature says the effect has already decayed.

spec.doa_line: Kill if, on the frozen long_1h train screen, n<30 OR bootstrap CI95 of net bps includes 0 OR observed WR < p*(150bps)=53.83% (fee_math.p_star), OR the ±20% tp_bps robustness read (STANDARDS #9: 120bps and 180bps variants) flips net_bps_mean sign in either variant.

import pandas as pd
from research.swarm.lib import load_data as ld


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Long-only: fires 1 when BTC's own PRIOR closed 1h bar returned below -60 bps, on the
    theory that this alt (ETH/SOL/XRP/ADA) overshoots the BTC-implied fair value during the
    liquidation-cascade panic and reverts upward over the following hours. Uses only BTC bars
    with ts <= the current alt bar's ts (merge_asof backward) and a 1-bar shift on BTC's own
    return, so no future information ever enters the signal at any prefix-truncation point.
    """
    btc = ld.load_ohlcv("BTC", "1h", era="train", dataset="long_1h")
    btc_ret_prior = btc["close"].pct_change().shift(1)

    b = btc_ret_prior.rename("btc_ret_prior").reset_index()
    b.columns = ["ts", "btc_ret_prior"]
    b = b.sort_values("ts")

    alt_ts = pd.DataFrame({"ts": df.index}).sort_values("ts")
    merged = pd.merge_asof(alt_ts, b, on="ts", direction="backward")
    merged = merged.set_index("ts").reindex(df.index)

    thresh = -0.006
    sig = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    sig[merged["btc_ret_prior"] < thresh] = 1
    return sig
